effects.title: 3D Flip Card
effects.summary: A card flips on hover/focus to reveal its back face in 3D.
effects.description: Uses perspective on the scene, transform-style: preserve-3d on the rotating inner element, and backface-visibility: hidden on two stacked faces to create the classic 3D card flip.
effects.accessibility_notes: Make it flip on :focus-within too (not only hover) so keyboard users can reach the back. Back content stays in the DOM. Disable/instant under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Flip on click via a toggled class
effects.ai_usage: Use for flashcards, team bios, before/after, pricing toggles. Structure: .scene (perspective) > .card (preserve-3d, rotateY on hover) > .face.front + .face.back (both position:absolute, backface-visibility:hidden; back pre-rotated 180deg). Trigger with :hover AND :focus-within for keyboard access. For click-to-flip, toggle a class instead.

effects.title: Rotating 3D Pyramid
effects.summary: A square-based pyramid spins in 3D space, built from four triangular CSS faces.
effects.description: Four clip-path triangles are hinged at a square base and folded up to a shared apex inside a preserve-3d scene, then spun on a loop — pure-CSS 3D, no libraries.
effects.performance_notes: Five layers + continuous rotation; cheap standalone. Avoid many at once.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative; pauses to a static pose under prefers-reduced-motion.

customization.name: --s
customization.description: Base edge length (scales the whole solid)

variations: Map a texture onto each face
effects.ai_usage: Eye-catching hero/showcase element. Each triangular face is clip-path polygon(50% 0,100% 100%,0 100%) with transform-origin at its bottom-centre, placed with rotateY(k*90deg) translateZ(--s/2) rotateX(--beta). For all four apexes to meet on the axis, --beta must satisfy --L*sin(--beta) = --s/2; here the proportions are fixed (height ≈ 0.85*edge) so the slant --L ≈ 0.986*--s and --beta ≈ 30.47deg are precomputed constants — scale the solid with --s alone. Wrap in a perspective scene with transform-style:preserve-3d and animate rotateY. Pause under reduced motion.

effects.title: Rotating Octahedron
effects.summary: A regular octahedron (eight equilateral triangles) spins in pure-CSS 3D.
effects.description: Two four-sided pyramids share an equator square — eight clip-path triangles inside a preserve-3d scene, spun on a loop. No libraries.
effects.performance_notes: Eight layers + continuous rotation; cheap standalone.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative; pauses to a static pose under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: Regular octahedron = two square-based pyramids sharing an equator. Build a top cap of four equilateral faces (clip-path polygon(50% 0,100% 100%,0 100%)) hinged at the equator: rotateY(k*90deg) translateZ(--s/2) rotateX(--beta) with --beta = 90deg - atan(sqrt(2)) ≈ 35.264deg (so --L*sin(--beta)=--s/2, --L≈0.866*--s). Mirror it with a second group set to rotateX(180deg) for the bottom cap. Scale with --s. Wrap in a perspective preserve-3d scene, animate rotateY, pause under reduced motion.

effects.title: Rotating Tetrahedron
effects.summary: A regular tetrahedron (four equilateral triangles) spins in pure-CSS 3D.
effects.description: Three clip-path triangles are hinged at a triangular base and folded up to a shared apex inside a preserve-3d scene, closed by a flat base face and spun on a loop.
effects.performance_notes: Four layers + continuous rotation; cheap standalone.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative; pauses to a static pose under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: Regular tetrahedron in pure CSS. Three equilateral side faces (clip-path polygon(50% 0,100% 100%,0 100%)) hinge at their bottom edge: rotateY(k*120deg) translateZ(--r) rotateX(--beta) with --r = inradius of the base triangle ≈ 0.2887*--s and --beta ≈ 19.471deg (so --L*sin(--beta)=--r, --L≈0.866*--s). The base is the same triangle laid flat with rotateX(90deg) about its centroid (transform-origin 50% 66.67%). Scale with --s. Wrap in a perspective preserve-3d scene, animate rotateY, pause under reduced motion.

effects.title: Animated Gradient Background
effects.summary: A smooth multi-color gradient that slowly drifts across the viewport.
effects.description: An oversized linear-gradient with background-size 400% and an animated background-position produces an endlessly shifting color wash — the ubiquitous SaaS hero background.
effects.performance_notes: Animating background-position is cheap; no JS. Long duration keeps repaints infrequent.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative. Keep foreground text contrast high across all gradient stops. Animation stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Pair with a noise overlay for texture
effects.ai_usage: Drop on a hero section or full page. Apply .animated-gradient to a full-size container; set background-size:400% 400% and animate background-position between corners. Use 3-4 harmonious colors. For readable text, overlay a semi-transparent dark layer or constrain text to a contrasted card. Keep duration long (12-20s) for an ambient feel.

effects.title: Animated Static
effects.summary: Pure white noise regenerated every few frames on a canvas.
effects.description: Writing random bytes into ImageData produces genuine per-pixel static that no CSS texture can match.
effects.performance_notes: Regenerating ImageData is the expensive part — render at a quarter resolution and scale up, and throttle to ~12fps.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: No-signal screens, error states, and analog aesthetics. Draw into a small offscreen canvas (e.g. 160×90) and let CSS scale it — full-resolution noise wastes an enormous amount of fill rate for no visual gain.

effects.title: Animated Wave Divider
effects.summary: A gently rolling SVG wave that separates two sections.
effects.description: An inline SVG wave path sits at a section boundary; a duplicated path translates horizontally on a loop to make the crest roll — the popular section-divider flourish.
effects.performance_notes: Animating translateX on an SVG path is cheap. Use a wide path (≥200% width) and shift by one wavelength for a seamless loop.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative (SVG aria-hidden). Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion (static wave).
variations: Layer two waves at different speeds/opacity for depth
Flip vertically for a top divider
effects.ai_usage: Use to transition between two colored sections. Place an SVG wave (path filled with --wave) at the boundary; make the path wider than the viewport and animate translateX by exactly one wavelength for a seamless roll. Layer 2-3 waves with different speeds/opacities for parallax depth. Mark the SVG aria-hidden and disable motion under reduced-motion. Match --wave to the next section's background.

effects.title: Argyle
effects.summary: Diamonds with crossing overcheck lines, knitwear style.
effects.description: A diamond lattice from two 45° gradient sets plus dashed diagonal overchecks, the way the pattern is actually knitted.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Remove the overcheck for plain harlequin
effects.ai_usage: Fashion, golf, and preppy branding. The dashed overcheck lines at 45° are what distinguishes argyle from a plain harlequin diamond grid — do not omit them.

effects.title: Aurora Background
effects.summary: Soft, blurred color blobs drift like northern lights behind your content.
effects.description: Several large radial-gradient blobs are blurred heavily and animated on independent paths over a dark base, creating a calm aurora/northern-lights ambience popular in modern landing pages.
effects.browser_support: All modern browsers (filter: blur widely supported).
effects.performance_notes: Large blur radii are GPU-intensive; limit to 2-3 blobs and avoid animating blur itself (animate transform instead).
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative; keep content on a contrasted surface. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Tighter, brighter blobs for a nebula
Add grain overlay for film texture
effects.ai_usage: Use as a calm, premium hero/section background on dark UIs. Place the .aurora container behind content (position relative, content with higher z-index). Each blob is an absolutely-positioned blurred radial-gradient; animate their transform (translate) on long, offset loops. Keep blob count low for performance and pick 2-3 analogous-but-distinct colors.

effects.title: Aurora Ribbons
effects.summary: Vertical light curtains sway and change colour.
effects.description: Tall blurred gradient columns skew and translate independently, producing the curtain motion aurora photos actually show.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: Night, arctic, and dreamy themes. Curtains must be vertical, blurred, and skewed — a horizontal blurred gradient reads as a sunset, not an aurora.

effects.title: Blueprint Grid
effects.summary: Cyan draughting paper with fine and heavy rules.
effects.description: Two grid layers at different scales — a fine 20px cell and a heavy 100px major line — read exactly like technical paper.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Add a title block in the corner
Animate a drawing reveal over it
effects.ai_usage: Engineering, planning, and 'work in progress' pages. Layer a 1px fine grid under a 2px major grid at 5× the size — a single grid always reads as graph paper rather than a blueprint.

effects.title: Bokeh Lights
effects.summary: Out-of-focus light circles drift at different depths.
effects.description: Blur and opacity scale with each circle's size, so the smaller, sharper lights read as nearer than the large soft ones.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Mask to the hero area only
effects.ai_usage: Warm, premium hero backdrops. Vary blur, size, and speed together — uniform blur across all circles flattens the depth illusion instantly.

effects.title: Brick Wall
effects.summary: Staggered brick courses with mortar gaps.
effects.description: Two identical brick layers offset by half a brick and half a course produce the running bond a single layer cannot.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: Industrial, cafe, and loft aesthetics. The running bond comes from a second gradient pair offset by half the brick width and half the course height — without that offset the wall reads as a plain grid.

effects.title: Carbon Fibre
effects.summary: A woven carbon-fibre weave from four tiny gradients.
effects.description: Two pairs of 45° gradients offset by half a tile create the over-under weave that a single gradient cannot.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Larger weave for a coarser look
effects.ai_usage: Automotive, audio, and hardware skins. Keep the tile small (8–14px); larger tiles expose the gradient trick and stop reading as material.

effects.title: Checkerboard
effects.summary: A classic two-tone checker built from two offset conic gradients.
effects.description: One conic-gradient tile with four quadrants tiles into a perfect checker at any size.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: Transparency indicators, retro sections, and image placeholders. conic-gradient(#a 0 25%, #b 0 50%, #a 0 75%, #b 0) with background-size: 2×square is the shortest correct checker in CSS.

effects.title: Circuit Board
effects.summary: PCB traces and pads etched across a dark board.
effects.description: Right-angle gradient traces plus a dot layer for vias produce a plausible circuit without drawing a single path.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Animate a pulse along the traces
Denser grid for a busier board
effects.ai_usage: Hardware, embedded, and hacker aesthetics. Mixing a square grid with an offset dot grid is what sells it — traces alone read as graph paper.

effects.title: Corner Mesh
effects.summary: Four corner colour sources blending across the viewport.
effects.description: Four corner colour sources blending across the viewport.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep text contrast above 4.5:1 and stop drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: The standard mesh-gradient hero. Anchor one radial per corner and keep each under 55% reach so the centre stays dark enough for text.

effects.title: CRT Scanlines
effects.summary: Fine scanlines plus a rolling refresh bar over a curved vignette.
effects.description: Three cues stack: hard scanlines, a slow rolling band, and a corner vignette — together they read as a CRT rather than a striped overlay.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Stronger curvature with a radial mask
effects.ai_usage: Retro-terminal and arcade skins. Put this layer above your content with pointer-events:none; the rolling bar should be very subtle (opacity < .06) or it becomes a distraction rather than an artefact.

effects.title: Diagonal Stripes
effects.summary: Repeating 45° stripes that drift slowly sideways.
effects.description: repeating-linear-gradient supplies the stripes; the drift is a background-position animation matched exactly to the stripe period.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Higher contrast for a barber pole
Freeze the drift for a static texture
effects.ai_usage: Section backgrounds and empty states. Animate background-position by exactly 2× the stripe width (the gradient period) or the loop visibly jumps.

effects.title: Dot Grid Background
effects.summary: An evenly spaced dotted grid drawn with a single repeating radial-gradient.
effects.description: One radial-gradient tile repeated via background-size produces a clean polka/dot grid — the understated backdrop seen in note apps and design canvases.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative; keep dots subtle.
variations: Offset rows for a diamond layout
effects.ai_usage: Subtle backdrop for canvases, note apps, and minimal sites. Apply .dot-bg. The dot is radial-gradient(var(--dot) var(--r), transparent var(--r)); background-size:--size sets spacing. Adjust --r vs --size ratio for density. Works on light or dark by changing --dot.

effects.title: Dot Grid Spotlight
effects.summary: A subtle dot-grid background that lights up only within a soft circle following the cursor.
effects.description: A faint dot grid covers the section; a brighter copy is revealed through a radial mask centered on the pointer, so the grid 'illuminates' around the cursor. A clean, techy hero backdrop seen across modern dev/SaaS sites.
effects.browser_support: All modern browsers (CSS mask, custom properties).
effects.performance_notes: One pointermove updates --mx/--my; the grid is a repeating radial-gradient (cheap). Spotlight hides under reduced-motion / no-pointer.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative only; foreground content keeps its own contrast. No keyboard dependency.
effects.ai_usage: Use as a hero/section backdrop for dev/SaaS/AI sites. Render a dim repeating-radial-gradient dot grid; overlay a brighter identical grid masked by a radial-gradient at --mx/--my (updated on pointermove) so dots brighten near the cursor. Tune --gap and --r. Keep content above it; the spotlight is decorative, so it's fine to hide it when no pointer or under reduced motion.
effects.source: Move your cursor ✦

effects.title: Dot Wave Field
effects.summary: A grid of dots whose scale ripples outward in a wave.
effects.description: Per-dot delays computed from distance to the centre make the ripple radiate instead of sweeping in rows.
effects.performance_notes: Roughly 100 small elements animating transform only — fine, but do not scale this to thousands of dots.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: Interactive hero sections and data-flavoured backdrops. Compute the delay from the dot's distance to the wave origin — a linear index delay produces a diagonal sweep, not a circular ripple.

effects.title: Drifting Mesh
effects.summary: Soft colour nodes drift behind a heavy blur, never repeating exactly.
effects.description: Four blurred nodes on coprime durations mean the composition takes minutes to repeat, unlike a looping gradient.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Freeze at a pleasing frame for a static export
effects.ai_usage: Premium marketing backgrounds. Use durations that are not multiples of each other (17s, 23s, 29s) so the loop point is imperceptible; add a grain overlay to hide gradient banding on wide screens.

effects.title: Fading Grid
effects.summary: A technical grid that dissolves toward the edges.
effects.description: A radial mask over the grid keeps the centre crisp and the periphery clean, so foreground text stays readable.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: The default SaaS hero backdrop. The mask is what makes it usable: radial-gradient(ellipse at center, #000 40%, transparent 75%) prevents the grid from fighting with content at the edges.

effects.title: Film Grain Overlay
effects.summary: An animated grain layer that sits over any content.
effects.description: A tiled SVG turbulence texture jitters between eight positions, so the grain resamples like real film rather than sitting still.
effects.performance_notes: One tiled texture with a stepped transform — cheaper than re-generating noise per frame. Keep opacity low.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Colored grain for a processing error look
effects.ai_usage: Overlay this on photos, videos, or whole pages to kill digital flatness. Use pointer-events:none and mix-blend-mode:overlay, and step the transform (steps(8)) instead of easing — smooth motion looks like a moving texture, not grain.

effects.title: Floating Geometry
effects.summary: Outlined squares, circles, and triangles drift upward at different rates.
effects.description: Each shape has its own duration, delay, and rotation, so the field never resolves into a visible loop.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Filled shapes for a bolder look
Drift sideways for a marquee feel
effects.ai_usage: Landing-page sections that need life without distraction. Keep stroke-only shapes at low opacity, and give every shape a unique duration — matched durations make the whole field pulse as one.

effects.title: Floating Particles
effects.summary: Drifting glowing dots rise gently across the background, generated with a little JS.
effects.description: A small script spawns N absolutely-positioned dots with randomized size, position, and animation duration; CSS floats them upward in a loop for an ambient particle field.
effects.performance_notes: Keep particle count modest (≈30-60). Each animates transform/opacity only. For hundreds of particles, switch to canvas.
effects.accessibility_notes: Purely decorative; the script skips animation when prefers-reduced-motion is set (renders static dots).
variations: Connect nearby particles with lines via canvas
effects.ai_usage: Ambient atmosphere behind heroes. The JS loop creates COUNT dots with random left%, size, delay, and duration, appended to a relative container. CSS animates translateY upward + fade. Keep count low for DOM-based; escalate to canvas for dense fields. Always behind content (z-index) and behind the reduced-motion guard.

effects.title: Folded Paper
effects.summary: Soft creases divide the surface into folded panels.
effects.description: Alternating light and shadow gradients along fold lines imply a sheet that has been folded and flattened.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: Editorial, packaging, and invitation designs. Fold lines need both a highlight and a shadow immediately adjacent — a single dark line reads as a printed rule, not a crease.

effects.title: Framed Gradient Edge
effects.summary: A luminous gradient frame hugs the viewport edges.
effects.description: A masked gradient border on a fixed overlay draws attention inward without touching the content layer.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep contrast with foreground text above 4.5:1 and disable drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: Recording indicators, focus modes, and live states. The mask-composite trick (two masks, xor) is the portable way to show only the border of a gradient-filled box.

effects.title: Grainy Gradient
effects.summary: A smooth gradient with grain to kill banding.
effects.description: A smooth gradient with grain to kill banding.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative surface — keep text contrast above 4.5:1 and stop drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: Any large gradient on a wide screen. A 25–35% noise overlay is the standard fix for the visible stepping that 8-bit gradients produce.

effects.title: Grainy Gradient Background
effects.summary: A slowly drifting multi-color gradient mesh with an SVG film-grain overlay for a tactile, premium finish.
effects.description: Pairs two 2026 staples: an animated gradient mesh (Aurora-style) and a noise/grain texture. The grain (an inline SVG feTurbulence) breaks up banding and adds an analog, expensive feel over the smooth gradient.
effects.browser_support: All modern browsers (SVG filters, CSS animation).
effects.performance_notes: The grain is a tiled static SVG data-URI (cheap); only the gradient position animates. Animation pauses under reduced-motion.
effects.accessibility_notes: Purely decorative; ensure foreground text has its own contrast. Grain opacity kept low to avoid distraction.
variations: Heavier grain for a poster look
effects.ai_usage: Use as a hero/section background that feels premium and avoids flat gradient banding. Layer: animated multi-radial gradient on the base, then a tiled SVG feTurbulence grain (data-URI) on top at low opacity (~0.05–0.1) with mix-blend overlay. Recolor via --c1..--c3. Keep text contrast independent of the background and pause the drift under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.source: Grainy gradient ✶

effects.title: Grid Lines Background
effects.summary: A crisp blueprint/graph-paper grid drawn entirely with a repeating gradient.
effects.description: Two linear-gradients (one per axis) with a fixed background-size create an infinite grid. A radial mask fades the edges for a focused, tech-y backdrop.
effects.browser_support: All modern browsers; the edge fade uses mask-image (well supported, prefix for older Safari).
effects.performance_notes: Pure CSS tiling, no animation — free.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative; keep grid faint so it doesn't reduce text contrast.
effects.ai_usage: Use behind dashboards, dev tools, and tech landing pages. Apply .grid-bg to a full container. effects.title: 3D Press Button
effects.summary: A chunky button with a solid bottom edge that depresses satisfyingly when clicked.
effects.description: A box-shadow acts as the button's 3D side; on :active the button translates down and the shadow shrinks, simulating a physical key press.

effects.accessibility_notes: Real <button>; the press also triggers on keyboard activation focus state. Transition is short and not motion-sickness inducing, but is reduced under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Pill radius for a candy button
effects.ai_usage: Use for playful, game-like, or kid-friendly UIs. The 3D edge is a single box-shadow of height --depth in the --edge color. On :active, translateY(--depth) and remove the shadow so the button 'sinks'. Keep the transition fast (~60ms) for tactile feel. Pair --edge as a darker shade of --face.

<!DOCTYPE html>

<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />

  <script type="application/json" id="effect-meta">
  {
    "id": "press-3d-button",
    "title": "3D Press Button",
    "summary": "A chunky button with a solid bottom edge that depresses satisfyingly when clicked.",
    "description": "A box-shadow acts as the button's 3D side; on :active the button translates down and the shadow shrinks, simulating a physical key press.",
    "theme": "buttons",
    "categories": ["button", "3d", "skeuomorphic"],
    "tags": ["3d", "press", "tactile", "box-shadow", "playful", "skeuomorphic"],
    "tech": ["css"],
    "era": "2020s",
    "difficulty": "beginner",
    "dependencies": [],
    "browser_support": "All modern browsers.",
    "performance_notes": "Animates transform + box-shadow on :active; trivial cost.",
    "accessibility_notes": "Real <button>; the press also triggers on keyboard activation focus state. Transition is short and not motion-sickness inducing, but is reduced under prefers-reduced-motion.",
    "customization": [
      { "name": "--face", "description": "Top face color", "default": "#22d3ee" },
      { "name": "--edge", "description": "Bottom edge color (darker)", "default": "#0e7490" },
      { "name": "--depth", "description": "How thick the 3D edge is", "default": "6px" }
    ],
    "variations": ["Pill radius for a candy button", "Larger --depth for arcade buttons", "Color-shift the face on hover"],
    "related": ["ripple-button"],
    "ai_usage": "Use for playful, game-like, or kid-friendly UIs. The 3D edge is a single box-shadow of height --depth in the --edge color. On :active, translateY(--depth) and remove the shadow so the button 'sinks'. Keep the transition fast (~60ms) for tactile feel. Pair --edge as a darker shade of --face."
  }
  </script>
  <style>
    :root { --face: #22d3ee; --edge: #0e7490; --depth: 6px; }
    html, body { height: 100%; margin: 0; }
    body { display: grid; place-items: center; background: #0b0d12; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; }

      border: none; cursor: pointer; color: #042f3a; font-weight: 800; font-size: 1.05rem;

effects.title: Animated Gradient Border
effects.summary: A button (or card) wrapped in a conic gradient border that rotates, with a soft matching glow.
effects.description: A rotating conic-gradient sits behind the element and is revealed only as a ring via a masked inset, so the border appears to spin. A blurred copy underneath adds a glow. Popular on AI/dev product CTAs and pricing 'featured' cards.
effects.browser_support: Uses @property for smooth angle animation (Chromium/Safari/FF current); degrades to a static gradient where unsupported.
effects.performance_notes: One animated custom property driving a conic-gradient + a blurred glow layer. Pause on reduced-motion.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative border; keep the inner element a real button with focus-visible and adequate contrast.
variations: Reveal the spin only on hover
effects.ai_usage: Use to make a CTA or 'most popular' card stand out on AI/dev/SaaS sites. Put a rotating conic-gradient on a wrapper, then mask its center so only a ring shows (border); duplicate it blurred underneath for glow. Animate the angle via an @property <angle> custom property for a smooth spin. Keep the inner button accessible and pause under prefers-reduced-motion.

effects.title: Animated Gradient Border Button

effects.description: Uses an animated @property angle driving a conic-gradient background, with a mask/inset technique so only the border shows. Falls back gracefully where @property is unsupported.
effects.browser_support: Best in Chromium/Safari/Firefox 2023+. @property animation of the angle degrades to a static gradient in older browsers.
effects.performance_notes: Animating a registered custom property (angle) is compositor-friendly. One element + one pseudo.
effects.accessibility_notes: Real <button>; focus-visible ring retained. Border rotation stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Pause rotation, spin on hover only
effects.ai_usage: Use for premium CTAs. Technique: the button background is a conic-gradient(from var(--angle), ...); a ::before with the solid --bg color is inset by the border width to reveal only the ring. Register @property --angle as <angle> and animate it 0→360deg. If you can't use @property, replace with a static linear-gradient border via the border-image or padding-box/border-box double-background trick.

effects.ai_usage: Attach to any real <button>. The JS computes click coordinates relative to the button, sizes the ripple to cover it (diameter = max(width,height)), and removes the node on animationend. Requires position:relative + overflow:hidden on the button. Reuse the addRipple() function for multiple buttons by delegating or looping over a selector.
effects.source:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
  <title>Material Ripple Button</title>
  <script type="application/json" id="effect-meta">
  {
    "id": "ripple-button",
    "title": "Material Ripple Button",
    "summary": "A circular ripple expands from the click point, the classic Material Design touch feedback.",
    "description": "On pointer down, a span is positioned at the cursor and scaled up while fading out, creating the ink-ripple. Vanilla JS, no framework.",
    "theme": "buttons",
    "categories": ["button", "feedback", "interaction"],
    "tags": ["ripple", "material", "click", "feedback", "wave"],
    "tech": ["css", "js"],
    "era": "2010s",
    "difficulty": "intermediate",
    "dependencies": [],
    "browser_support": "All modern browsers.",
    "performance_notes": "Each click spawns one short-lived element that is removed on animationend — no leaks.",
    "accessibility_notes": "Purely additive visual feedback over a real <button>; keyboard activation still works. Honors prefers-reduced-motion by skipping the ripple.",
    "customization": [
      { "name": "--ripple", "description": "Ripple ink color", "default": "rgba(255,255,255,.6)" },
      { "name": "background", "description": "Button base color", "default": "#7c5cff" }
    ],
    "variations": ["Centered ripple for icon buttons", "Dark ripple on light buttons", "Slower ripple for a softer feel"],
    "related": ["gradient-border-button", "press-3d-button"],
    "ai_usage": "Attach to any real <button>. The JS computes click coordinates relative to the button, sizes the ripple to cover it (diameter = max(width,height)), and removes the node on animationend. Requires position:relative + overflow:hidden on the button. Reuse the addRipple() function for multiple buttons by delegating or looping over a selector."
  }
  </script>
  <style>
    html, body { height: 100%; margin: 0; }
    body { display: grid; place-items: center; background: #0b0d12; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; }
    .ripple-btn {
      --ripple: rgba(255,255,255,.6);
      position: relative; overflow: hidden;
      border: none; cursor: pointer;
      padding: 0.95rem 2.4rem; border-radius: 12px;
      font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; color: #fff;
      background: #7c5cff; box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(124,92,255,.4);
    }
    .ripple-btn span.ink {
      position: absolute; border-radius: 50%; transform: scale(0);
      background: var(--ripple); pointer-events: none;
      animation: ripple 0.6s linear;
    }
    @keyframes ripple { to { transform: scale(2.5); opacity: 0; } }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ripple-btn span.ink { display: none; } }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button class="ripple-btn" id="btn">Click me</button>
  <script>
    function addRipple(e) {
      var btn = e.currentTarget;
      var rect = btn.getBoundingClientRect();
      var size = Math.max(rect.width, rect.height);
      var ink = document.createElement("span");
      ink.className = "ink";
      ink.style.width = ink.style.height = size + "px";
      ink.style.left = (e.clientX - rect.left - size / 2) + "px";
      ink.style.top = (e.clientY - rect.top - size / 2) + "px";
      btn.appendChild(ink);
      ink.addEventListener("animationend", function () { ink.remove(); });
    }
    document.getElementById("btn").addEventListener("click", addRipple);
  </script>
</body>
</html>

effects.title: WCAG Contrast Grid
effects.summary: Every foreground/background pair in a palette, scored against WCAG 2.1 contrast thresholds and labelled AAA / AA / AA-Large / fail.
effects.description: A palette is only usable in the combinations that actually pass contrast, and that is not obvious by eye — mid-tone accents on dark surfaces fail far more often than designers expect. This specimen takes a set of tokens, computes the real WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio for every foreground-on-background pair, and renders the matrix with each cell showing its ratio and grade. The maths is the spec formula, not an approximation: sRGB channels are linearised, relative luminance is weighted 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722, and the ratio is (L_light + 0.05) / (L_dark + 0.05).
effects.browser_support: All modern browsers. Plain DOM and arithmetic, no color-space APIs required.
effects.performance_notes: One pass over N×N pairs at load; a 6-token palette is 36 cells. Nothing animates and nothing recomputes unless the palette changes.
effects.accessibility_notes: The grid is a real table with scope-ed headers, so it reads correctly in a screen reader. Grade is never carried by colour alone — every cell states its ratio and its grade as text. Note WCAG 2.1 ratios ignore how the eye actually responds at low luminance; APCA (WCAG 3 draft) scores dark-mode pairs more faithfully, so treat a bare pass on dark surfaces as a floor, not a target.

customization.name: PALETTE
customization.description: The tokens to cross-check — swap in your own name/hex pairs

customization.name: thresholds
customization.description: WCAG 2.1 cutoffs: 7 = AAA, 4.5 = AA, 3 = AA Large (18pt+/14pt bold) and non-text UI

variations: Restrict rows to text tokens and columns to surface tokens — the pairs you would actually ship
Emit the failures as a build-time check that fails CI when a shipped pair regresses
Score with APCA instead for dark-heavy interfaces
Add a column for the smallest passing font size per pair
effects.ai_usage:
Use this to audit a palette BEFORE committing tokens, and to answer 'can I put this colour on that one'. Drop your tokens into PALETTE as {name, hex} and read the matrix.

The formula, if you are reimplementing it: convert each sRGB channel to 0–1, linearise with c <= 0.03928 ? c/12.92 : ((c+0.055)/1.055)^2.4, take L = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B, then ratio = (Llighter + 0.05) / (Ldarker + 0.05). Ratio runs 1 (identical) to 21 (black on white). Thresholds: 4.5 for body text (AA), 7 for AAA, 3 for large text (18pt / 14pt bold) and for non-text UI such as icons, focus rings, and input borders.

Apply it: body copy needs 4.5 minimum — do not ship a 3.2 accent as a text colour just because it looks fine to you on a calibrated display. Placeholder text, disabled states, and thin icon strokes are the usual silent failures. Contrast is symmetric, so the matrix is mirrored; you only need one triangle.

Caveats worth passing on: WCAG 2.1 is known to be lenient on dark backgrounds and harsh on mid-tones, so a 4.6 on a near-black surface can still read poorly — prefer APCA there. And never encode pass/fail in colour alone in your own UI; state the number.
effects.source: WCAG 2.1 contrast — foreground (row) on background (column)

effects.title: Site Footer Block
effects.summary: A complete multi-column site footer — brand, link columns, newsletter capture, social row, and a legal bar.
effects.description: The block every site needs and no component library ships well. Four link columns and a brand block sit in an auto-fitting grid that collapses to a single column on narrow screens without a media query, a newsletter field pairs input and button on one row, and a legal bar carries copyright, locale, and the policy links that have to be one click from every page. Link hover uses a background-size underline sweep rather than text-decoration so it animates, and the whole block is one <footer> with real nav landmarks.
effects.browser_support: All modern browsers. The link columns reflow on width via grid auto-fit + minmax with no JS; a single max-width query drops the brand above the columns on phones.
effects.performance_notes: Static layout, no animation beyond link hover transitions on background-size. Nothing here triggers layout on interaction.
effects.accessibility_notes: Link groups are <nav> landmarks with aria-label so screen-reader users can skip between them, and each column heading is a real <h2> the groups are labelled by. The newsletter input has a visually-hidden <label> rather than a placeholder standing in for one. Muted link text is held at 4.5:1 against the footer surface — footers are where contrast most often quietly fails.

Add a locale/currency switcher to the legal bar

Add a status-page indicator dot beside the brand
effects.ai_usage:
Drop-in site footer. Use it as the closing block of a marketing site, docs site, or app shell; it is deliberately generic so you can delete columns rather than invent them.

Structure to keep: one <footer> landmark, each link group a <nav aria-label> containing a real heading, the newsletter input paired with a visually-hidden <label> (a placeholder is not a label — it vanishes on focus and many screen readers skip it), and the legal bar last.

Layout gotcha worth copying exactly: the brand block and the link columns are TWO nested grids. If you put the brand in the same repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...)) row as the nav columns, the brand track absorbs the free space, auto-fit resolves to a single track, and every column stacks into one tall list. Keep .cols as its own grid so auto-fit only measures the columns.

Tune: --surface one step off your page background so the footer reads as a distinct region, --muted at or above 4.5:1 against it, and --accent for hover plus the button. Raise the minmax floor if your link labels are long, or columns will wrap mid-word.

Avoid: burying the privacy/terms links (they must be reachable from every page), using placeholder text as the newsletter label, dropping muted text below 4.5:1 because 'it is only the footer' — that is the single most common contrast failure on a shipped site — and stuffing every route in here. Four columns of six links is the practical ceiling before it becomes a sitemap nobody reads.

effects.title: Glyph Field
effects.summary: A canvas grid of ASCII glyphs ignites under the pointer, pointing the way you moved and heating up as you go faster.
effects.description: A full-bleed monospace grid sits behind the page. Pointer movement stamps a capsule of intensity along the segment travelled, so fast flicks paint continuous ribbons instead of dotted samples. Each lit cell renders a glyph chosen from one of eight direction sets (>, \, v, /, <, ^ …), so the field reads as an arrow map of your gesture. Cursor speed drives a separate heat channel that ramps the glyph color from a cold ink tone to a hot accent, and a click launches an expanding ring whose glyphs face outward from the impact. Cells decay and cool on their own, so the trail dissolves a moment after you stop.
effects.browser_support: Any browser with Canvas 2D and Pointer Events (Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Safari). Gracefully renders a single static frame when reduced motion is requested or no fine pointer is present.
effects.performance_notes: State lives in Float32Array/Uint8Array grids indexed by cell, never per-cell objects. Only lit cells are visited (a compacted active list), draws are bucketed by font size x color band so fillStyle/font change at most SIZES*BANDS times per frame, and clearRect covers only the dirty rectangle rather than the full canvas. Device pixel ratio is capped at 1.5, the loop halves its rate while idle and stops entirely once the field is dark. Cost scales with the lit area, not the viewport.
effects.accessibility_notes: Purely decorative: the canvas is aria-hidden, has pointer-events: none, and never replaces the system cursor. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (or on coarse/no-hover pointers) the animation loop and pointer listeners are skipped entirely and one still frame is painted instead. Nothing is conveyed by the glyphs alone, and page content sits in a positioned layer above with normal contrast.

customization.description: Per-frame multipliers for intensity and heat — lower fades faster

customization.description: Click ring expansion px/s, band thickness, and travel before it dies

variations: Swap SETS for katakana, braille (⠁⠂⠄⡀), or box-drawing characters for a different alphabet
Drop the direction buckets and always use one glyph set for a plain heat trail
Drive the field from scroll velocity instead of the pointer
Constrain the canvas to a hero section (position: absolute inside a relative parent) instead of the viewport
Emit a wave on route change or form submit rather than on click
effects.ai_usage:
Use for a decorative, tech-flavoured pointer trail behind a hero or landing page — terminal, developer-tool, AI, or cyber aesthetics. Do NOT use it as a cursor replacement (keep the native cursor) or on content-dense/text-heavy pages, where it competes with reading.

Integrate: put <canvas data-glyph-field aria-hidden="true"></canvas> first in <body>, style it position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 0; pointer-events: none, and give your content wrapper position: relative; z-index: 1 — without that the content sits at the same layer and the glyphs draw over it. The script self-initializes on DOM ready; window.GlyphField.init(canvas), .destroy(), and .refreshColors() are also exposed. In React/Vue/Next call init(ref.current) from an effect after mount and destroy() on unmount, and never call it during server rendering (it needs window). Only one instance is active at a time; init on a new canvas replaces the previous one.

Tune: set --glyph-field-cold and --glyph-field-hot on :root (they fall back to --ink/--accent, then built-in values) — cold should be close to your body text color and hot to your accent, or the trail turns into confetti. Root data-theme/class/style changes refresh automatically; call refreshColors() when theme state lives elsewhere. Raise R_BASE for a broader wash, lower DECAY for a snappier fade, and edit SETS to change the alphabet.

Avoid: giving the canvas pointer events or a positive z-index above content; removing the reduced-motion and fine-pointer gate; running one instance per component render; replacing the typed arrays with per-cell objects, clearing the whole canvas each frame, or removing the idle throttle and the 1.5 DPR cap — those four are what keep it cheap. Because it paints the full viewport behind everything, verify text contrast with the hot color at full intensity.

effects.title: Custom Range Slider
effects.summary: A styled range input with a gradient-filled track that follows the thumb.
effects.description: Styles the native <input type=range> thumb and track cross-browser, and uses a CSS variable updated on input to paint the filled portion of the track up to the current value.

effects.performance_notes: Updates one CSS var on input; trivial.
effects.accessibility_notes: Built on a real <input type=range>, so it is keyboard-operable (arrows) and announces value. Provide a <label> and aria-valuetext if the raw number needs units/context.
variations: Show a value tooltip above the thumb
effects.ai_usage: Use for volume, price, opacity, etc. Keep the native <input type=range> for accessibility; style ::-webkit-slider-thumb and ::-moz-range-thumb plus the track. For the filled portion, set a --fill percentage from JS on 'input' (value normalized to 0-100%) and paint the track with a linear-gradient hard-stop at --fill. Always pair with a <label>.
effects.source:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
  <title>Custom Range Slider</title>
  <script type="application/json" id="effect-meta">
  {
    "id": "custom-range-slider",
    "title": "Custom Range Slider",
    "summary": "A styled range input with a gradient-filled track that follows the thumb.",
    "description": "Styles the native <input type=range> thumb and track cross-browser, and uses a CSS variable updated on input to paint the filled portion of the track up to the current value.",
    "theme": "forms-inputs",
    "categories": ["form", "slider", "control"],
    "tags": ["range", "slider", "input", "fill", "thumb", "accessible"],
    "tech": ["css", "js"],
    "era": "2020s",
    "difficulty": "intermediate",
    "dependencies": [],
    "browser_support": "All modern browsers; thumb/track styling needs ::-webkit-slider-thumb and ::-moz-range-thumb.",
    "performance_notes": "Updates one CSS var on input; trivial.",
    "accessibility_notes": "Built on a real <input type=range>, so it is keyboard-operable (arrows) and announces value. Provide a <label> and aria-valuetext if the raw number needs units/context.",
    "customization": [
      { "name": "--accent", "description": "Filled track + thumb color", "default": "#7c5cff" },
      { "name": "--track", "description": "Empty track color", "default": "#2a3142" }
    ],
    "variations": ["Show a value tooltip above the thumb", "Stepped/ticked slider", "Dual-thumb range (needs two inputs)"],
    "related": ["before-after-slider", "toggle-switch"],
    "ai_usage": "Use for volume, price, opacity, etc. Keep the native <input type=range> for accessibility; style ::-webkit-slider-thumb and ::-moz-range-thumb plus the track. For the filled portion, set a --fill percentage from JS on 'input' (value normalized to 0-100%) and paint the track with a linear-gradient hard-stop at --fill. Always pair with a <label>."
  }
  </script>
  <style>
    :root { --accent: #7c5cff; --track: #2a3142; --fill: 50%; }
    html, body { height: 100%; margin: 0; }
    body { display: grid; place-items: center; background: #0b0d12; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; }
    .range {
      -webkit-appearance: none; appearance: none; width: 280px; height: 8px; border-radius: 999px; outline: none;
      background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--accent) var(--fill), var(--track) var(--fill));
    }
    .range::-webkit-slider-thumb { -webkit-appearance: none; appearance: none; width: 22px; height: 22px; border-radius: 50%;
      background: #fff; border: 3px solid var(--accent); cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.5); }
    .range::-moz-range-thumb { width: 22px; height: 22px; border-radius: 50%; background: #fff; border: 3px solid var(--accent); cursor: pointer; }
    .range:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 35%, transparent); }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <input class="range" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="50" aria-label="Volume" id="r" />
  <script>
    var r = document.getElementById("r");
    function paint() { r.style.setProperty("--fill", ((r.value - r.min) / (r.max - r.min) * 100) + "%"); }
    r.addEventListener("input", paint); paint();
  </script>
</body>
</html>

effects.title: File Drop Zone
effects.summary: Drag-and-drop upload area with a dashed target, live drag state, and a queued file list with progress bars.
effects.description: A drop target that is also a real file input, which is the part most implementations get wrong. The dashed frame lifts and tints on dragover, driven by a drag counter so that dragging across a child element does not flicker the state off and on. Dropped or picked files land in a queue with a type icon, a human-readable size, and a progress bar; the label wraps a visually-hidden <input type="file"> so the whole zone is clickable, focusable, and operable from the keyboard without a single extra listener.
effects.browser_support: All modern browsers. Drag-and-drop needs a pointer; the wrapped file input is the fallback everywhere else, including touch and keyboard.
effects.performance_notes: Listeners are bound once on the zone plus a window-level guard that stops the browser navigating away when a file is dropped outside it. Rendering is one row per file. Progress here is simulated on a timer — swap it for real XHR/fetch upload events.
effects.accessibility_notes: The zone is a <label> wrapping a visually-hidden (not display:none) file input, so it stays in the tab order, announces as a file control, and opens the picker on Enter or Space with no key handling of our own. Drag state is decorative only — every action is reachable without dragging. The queue is an aria-live="polite" region so added files are announced once. Focus is shown with a real outline, and the dashed border is not the only cue for the drag state.

customization.name: accept
customization.description: Restrict pickable types on the input; validate again on drop, since dropping bypasses accept

customization.name: MAX_MB
customization.description: Client-side size guard — always re-check server side

variations: Paste-to-upload by listening for paste and reading event.clipboardData.files
Image thumbnails via URL.createObjectURL, revoked on removal
Restrict to a single file and replace rather than append
effects.ai_usage:
Use for any file intake — attachments, avatar/logo upload, CSV import, document submission.

The one structural rule: the drop zone must wrap a real <input type="file">, hidden with the clip-rect visually-hidden pattern, NOT display:none or visibility:hidden — those remove it from the accessibility tree and the tab order, and you lose keyboard and touch users, who cannot drag anything. Wrapping it in a <label> gives you click-to-open, focus, and Enter/Space activation for free; do not reimplement those with key handlers.

Drag state: dragenter/dragleave fire for every child element, so track a depth counter (++ on enter, -- on leave, active while > 0) instead of toggling a boolean, or the highlight strobes. Call preventDefault in dragover or the drop never fires, and add a window-level dragover/drop guard so a missed drop does not navigate the page to the file.

Validate on both paths: the accept attribute filters the picker but does NOT filter drops, so re-check type and size in your drop handler, and re-check everything server side regardless. Progress here is a timer stub — replace it with xhr.upload.onprogress, or fetch with a streamed body, and handle failure per row rather than failing the whole queue.

Avoid: making drag the only way in, blocking the UI during upload, silently dropping files that exceed a limit (say which file and why), and forgetting to revoke object URLs if you add thumbnails.

effects.source:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
  <title>Magnetic Button</title>
  <script type="application/json" id="effect-meta">
  {
    "id": "magnetic-button",
    "title": "Magnetic Button",
    "summary": "A button that is gently pulled toward the cursor as it approaches, snapping back on exit.",
    "description": "Listens for pointer movement within a hit area and translates the button a fraction of the cursor offset, giving a magnetic, springy feel common in award-winning agency sites.",
    "theme": "hover-interactions",
    "categories": ["hover", "button", "micro-interaction"],
    "tags": ["magnetic", "cursor", "spring", "agency", "playful", "translate"],
    "tech": ["css", "js"],
    "era": "2020s",
    "difficulty": "intermediate",
    "dependencies": [],
    "browser_support": "All modern browsers with a pointer; on touch it simply does nothing special.",
    "performance_notes": "Transform-only updates on pointermove; smooth via a CSS transition for snap-back.",
    "accessibility_notes": "Pure enhancement; button works normally. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.",
    "customization": [
      { "name": "--strength", "description": "Pull factor (0-1)", "default": "0.4" }
    ],
    "variations": ["Magnetize the label separately from the button for layered pull", "Stronger pull for big hero CTAs", "Add scale on hover"],
    "related": ["tilt-card", "spotlight-card"],
    "ai_usage": "Use for hero CTAs and nav items on expressive, agency-style sites. Compute the cursor offset from the button center and translate the button by offset * strength on pointermove; reset transform to 0 on pointerleave (a CSS transition makes the snap-back springy). Keep strength ~0.2-0.4. Skip on touch and under reduced-motion."
  }
  </script>
  <style>
    html, body { height: 100%; margin: 0; }
    body { display: grid; place-items: center; background: #0b0d12; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; }
    .magnetic {
      border: none; cursor: pointer; color: #fff; font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.05rem;
      padding: 1.1rem 2.6rem; border-radius: 999px; background: #7c5cff;
      transition: transform .3s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1);
    }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .magnetic { transition: none; } }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button class="magnetic" id="btn">Magnetic</button>
  <script>
    var btn = document.getElementById("btn");
    var STRENGTH = 0.4;
    var reduce = matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;
    if (!reduce) {
      btn.addEventListener("pointermove", function (e) {
        var r = btn.getBoundingClientRect();
        var x = e.clientX - (r.left + r.width / 2);
        var y = e.clientY - (r.top + r.height / 2);
        btn.style.transform = "translate(" + x * STRENGTH + "px," + y * STRENGTH + "px)";
      });
      btn.addEventListener("pointerleave", function () { btn.style.transform = "translate(0,0)"; });
    }
  </script>
</body>
</html>

effects.title: Parallax Depth Card
effects.summary: Card layers shift by different amounts as the pointer moves.
effects.description: Each layer's translation is scaled by its own depth factor, so foreground elements outrun the background and the card gains real dimension.
effects.accessibility_notes: Every hover affordance here also responds to :focus-visible so keyboard users get the same information. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Add a tilt to the whole card
Depth on scroll instead of pointer
Shadow that moves opposite the layers
effects.ai_usage: Product and feature cards. Multiply the normalized pointer offset by a per-layer depth (0.2 → 1.0) and apply with translate3d; a single shared offset gives a slide, not parallax.

effects.title: Tilt + Spotlight Card
effects.summary: A card that tilts in 3D toward the cursor while a soft spotlight follows the pointer across its surface.
effects.description: Two effects in one interaction: the card rotates on X/Y based on pointer position (parallax depth), and a radial 'spotlight' highlight tracks the cursor via CSS custom properties. The signature hover for premium feature/pricing cards.
effects.browser_support: All modern browsers (CSS 3D transforms, custom properties).

variations: Stronger tilt for hero product shots
effects.ai_usage: Use for feature/pricing/product cards on premium landings. Set perspective on the parent; on pointermove map the cursor's position within the card to rotateX/rotateY (invert Y) and to a --mx/--my used by a radial-gradient spotlight overlay; reset on leave. Keep content above the spotlight layer, preserve focus order, and disable under reduced motion.

effects.title: Before / After Slider
effects.summary: Drag a handle to wipe between two images — the classic comparison slider.
effects.description: Two stacked images; a range input drives a CSS variable that clips the top image and positions a draggable divider, revealing the 'before' beneath the 'after'.
effects.performance_notes: Updates a CSS variable + clip on input; trivial.
effects.accessibility_notes: Built on a real <input type=range> so it's keyboard-operable and labelable — much better than a custom drag handler. Provide aria-label.
effects.ai_usage: Use for retouch/edit comparisons, product configurators, and map overlays. Stack two images; the top one is clipped via inset(0 calc(100% - var(--pos)) 0 0) (or clip-path). Drive --pos from a real range input's value (keyboard accessible) rather than custom mouse drag. Position the divider/handle at --pos. Replace the placeholder gradients with real before/after images and set alt text.
effects.source: BeforeAfter

effects.title: Blur-Up Image Load
effects.summary: The progressive 'blur-up': a tiny blurred placeholder sharpens into the full image as it loads — no layout jank, perceived speed.
effects.description: The LQIP / blur-up technique used by Next.js, Medium, and Unsplash: show a tiny, upscaled, blurred preview immediately, then crossfade to the sharp image on load. This demo simulates the load with a button so you can replay it.
effects.performance_notes: The placeholder is a tiny inline gradient/data-URI scaled up and blurred; swapping to the full image removes the blur. Reserve the box with aspect-ratio to avoid layout shift.
effects.accessibility_notes: Always give the real meaningful alt text; the blurred layer is aria-hidden. The box uses aspect-ratio so there's no CLS. Crossfade respects prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: Use for any content image to improve perceived performance and prevent layout shift. Wrap the image in a box with a fixed aspect-ratio; render a tiny LQIP (base64 or dominant color) scaled up + blurred behind it; when the full fires load, fade it in over the placeholder. Keep real alt text on the , aria-hide the placeholder, and respect reduced motion for the fade.
effects.source: Sharp image ✶

effects.title: Duotone Image
effects.summary: Recolor any photo into a two-tone gradient using blend modes.
effects.description: Desaturates the image and overlays a two-color gradient with mix-blend-mode so shadows take one color and highlights another — the Spotify-style duotone, done in CSS.
effects.browser_support: All modern browsers (mix-blend-mode, filter). For pixel-perfect duotone use SVG feColorMatrix.
effects.performance_notes: Blend modes + grayscale filter are GPU-accelerated; fine for hero images, avoid on large galleries.
effects.accessibility_notes: Heavy recoloring can hurt recognizability and contrast of any text baked into the image; keep alt text accurate.
effects.ai_usage: Brand-consistent photo treatment for heroes and cards. Wrap the image; apply filter:grayscale(1) contrast(1.1) to the ; overlay a ::after with linear-gradient(var(--shadow),var(--highlight)) and mix-blend-mode: screen (plus a multiply layer for richer results). Pick two brand colors (dark shadow, light highlight). For exact control, switch to an SVG feColorMatrix/feComponentTransfer filter.

customization.name: min column width

variations: auto-fill (keeps empty tracks) vs auto-fit (collapses them)

Choose MIN = the smallest acceptable card width; the grid computes column count per viewport with no media queries. Use auto-fit to collapse empty tracks (cards stretch), auto-fill to keep them. Add minmax(0,1fr) if long words overflow. Resize the frame to watch it reflow.

effects.title: Atom Orbits
effects.summary: Three elliptical rings on different axes with electrons riding each one.
effects.description: Rotating each flattened ellipse to a different angle fakes 3D orbits; the electrons are dots animated along the same rotation as their ring.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative status indicator — pair it with a visually-hidden aria-live message so screen readers announce the wait. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Add a glow to the nucleus
effects.ai_usage: Science, research, or 'computing' contexts. Each .ring is the same ellipse rotated 60° apart; the electron is a child positioned at the ellipse edge so it inherits the ring's rotation for free.

effects.title: Bouncing Dots
effects.summary: Three dots bounce in sequence — the friendly 'typing…' / loading indicator.
effects.description: Three dots share one bounce keyframe with staggered animation-delays so they rise and fall in a wave, evoking chat 'typing' indicators and lightweight loaders.
effects.accessibility_notes: Wrap with role=status + a label. Under prefers-reduced-motion, replace bounce with a gentle opacity pulse.
variations: More dots for a longer wave
effects.ai_usage: Use for chat 'typing' states and small inline loaders. Three .dot spans share a bounce animation with delays of 0, 0.16s, 0.32s. Tune --dot color and size. For reduced motion, swap the translateY bounce for an opacity pulse so it still signals activity without movement.

effects.title: Charging Battery
effects.summary: A battery fills in stages with a color that shifts from red to green.
effects.description: A single width animation drives the fill while a synchronized background-color keyframe walks the charge through danger, warning, and healthy hues.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative status indicator — pair it with a visually-hidden aria-live message so screen readers announce the wait. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Bind the width to a real percentage
effects.ai_usage: Device, power, or sync UIs. Two properties animate on one timeline (width and background-color) — keep their keyframe percentages aligned or the color changes at the wrong fill level. For real state, set width inline and drop the animation.

effects.title: Chat Typing Indicator
effects.summary: A message bubble with three dots that rise in sequence.
effects.description: The familiar chat affordance: a tail-bearing bubble plus three dots on a 0.18s stagger, sized to sit inline with real messages.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative status indicator — pair it with a visually-hidden aria-live message so screen readers announce the wait. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Add the sender's avatar beside it
Fade the whole bubble in on arrival
effects.ai_usage: Show it while awaiting a reply in chat or an AI stream. Match the bubble radius and padding to your real message bubbles so the indicator does not jump when the message replaces it; announce it with aria-live=polite.

effects.title: Checkerboard Loader
effects.summary: A 3×3 grid whose cells light up on a diagonal wave.
effects.description: Delays computed from each cell's row + column index make the highlight travel diagonally instead of row by row.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative status indicator — pair it with a visually-hidden aria-live message so screen readers announce the wait. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Scale cells as well as fade them
effects.ai_usage: Good for dashboard or data-heavy UIs where a round spinner looks out of place. The diagonal comes from animation-delay: calc((var(--r) + var(--c-i)) * .12s) — the same trick scales to any grid size.

effects.title: Circular Progress Ring
effects.summary: A determinate SVG ring that fills to a percentage via stroke-dashoffset, with a live label.
effects.description: An SVG circle whose stroke-dasharray equals its circumference; animating stroke-dashoffset reveals the arc proportional to a percentage — the standard circular progress meter.
effects.performance_notes: Animating stroke-dashoffset is cheap. For pure decoration use CSS; for real values update from JS.
effects.accessibility_notes: Add role=progressbar with aria-valuenow/min/max and keep the numeric label as text so the value is announced. Not just color — the number conveys the state.
effects.ai_usage: Use for upload/download progress, scores, and timers. circumference = 2*pi*r; set the circle's stroke-dasharray to that, and stroke-dashoffset = circumference * (1 - pct). Rotate the circle -90deg so it starts at top. Update offset + the text label + aria-valuenow from JS as progress changes. The demo animates 0→100% on a loop.

effects.title: Comet Spinner
effects.summary: A bright head chases its own fading tail around a circular track.
effects.description: A conic gradient supplies the fading tail while an absolutely positioned dot rides the leading edge, so the arc reads as a comet rather than a plain arc.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative status indicator — pair it with a visually-hidden aria-live message so screen readers announce the wait. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Slow the tail with a longer conic stop
Add a blur filter on the head for a softer glow
effects.ai_usage: Use as a premium-feeling spinner on dark surfaces. The rotation lives on the wrapper so head and tail stay locked together; the head dot is positioned at top center with transform-origin at the wrapper center.

effects.title: Conic Ring Spinner
effects.summary: A one-element ring spinner drawn with a conic gradient and a radial mask.
effects.description: A conic-gradient sweeps from transparent to the accent color; a radial-gradient mask punches out the middle, leaving a tapered arc that rotates.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative status indicator — pair it with a visually-hidden aria-live message so screen readers announce the wait. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Two stacked rings at different speeds
effects.ai_usage: Drop-in replacement for a border-based spinner when you want a tapered, gradient arc instead of a flat one. Apply .spin; --w is the stroke width and the mask must use the same value in calc(100% - var(--w)). Prefix the mask with -webkit-mask for Safari.

effects.title: Countdown Ring
effects.summary: An SVG ring that empties over a fixed duration with a digit at its center.
effects.description: stroke-dashoffset animates from zero to the full circumference, which drains the ring exactly once over --dur — the honest way to show a timed wait.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative status indicator — pair it with a visually-hidden aria-live message so screen readers announce the wait. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Turn red in the final second
effects.ai_usage: For timed waits with a known length — resend cooldowns, auto-redirects, session timeouts. Circumference is 2πr (here r=52 → 326.7); set stroke-dasharray to that number and animate stroke-dashoffset from 0 to it.

effects.description: A 3×3 grid pulsing in a diagonal wave.

effects.title: Domino Dots

effects.description: Each dot rotates about its bottom-left corner on a shared keyframe with a stepped delay, producing the chain-reaction read.

variations: Use squares for a more literal domino
Speed up the reset half of the cycle

effects.title: Dual Ring / Orbit Spinner

effects.description: A container and a pseudo-element each render an arc (colored border on opposing sides) and counter-rotate, producing an orbiting double-ring spinner.
effects.accessibility_notes: Pair with role=status + label. Slow down under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: A slightly fancier spinner for splash/loading screens. Outer element has border-top-color:--c1 and spins one way; ::after is an inset ring with border-bottom-color:--c2 spinning the other way. Keep within role=status and a hidden label. Size via --size.

effects.title: Folding Squares

effects.description: Four squares folding toward the centre in turn.

effects.description: A pulse with the double-beat rhythm of a heart.

effects.title: Hourglass
effects.summary: Sand drains from the top bulb to the bottom, then the whole glass flips.
effects.description: Two clipped triangles change height on the same timeline as a falling grain stream; a flip at the end of the cycle restarts it without a jump.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative status indicator — pair it with a visually-hidden aria-live message so screen readers announce the wait. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

Add grain speckles inside the sand
effects.ai_usage: Best for waits you can actually estimate — an hourglass implies finite time. The bulbs are clip-path triangles; animate the inner fill's height, and put the flip on the outer wrapper so the sand levels swap seamlessly.

effects.title: Indeterminate Progress Bar
effects.summary: A sliding accent segment loops across a track when progress can't be measured.
effects.description: A track contains a short bar that animates its position/width across, signaling ongoing work of unknown duration — the top-of-page loading bar pattern.
effects.performance_notes: Animates transform/left of one segment; cheap.
effects.accessibility_notes: Use role="progressbar" with aria-valuetext or an adjacent 'Loading' label; omit aria-valuenow when indeterminate. Animation continues under reduced-motion but you may slow it.
variations: Fix to top of viewport for route changes
effects.ai_usage: Use for unknown-duration tasks and page/route transitions (often pinned to the top of the viewport). The track is overflow:hidden; an inner segment animates from left:-40% to left:100%. Switch to a real determinate <progress> or a width-driven bar once you know the percentage. Set role=progressbar and a label.

effects.title: Infinity Loop
effects.summary: A dash travels an endless figure-eight path.
effects.description: One SVG path plus stroke-dasharray gives a short dash that runs the lemniscate forever, crossing itself at the middle.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative status indicator — pair it with a visually-hidden aria-live message so screen readers announce the wait. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Two dashes half a lap apart
Thicker stroke for a bolder mark
Gradient stroke via a linearGradient def
effects.ai_usage: A calm, brand-friendly loader for long operations. Change the dash length by editing the first stroke-dasharray value and keep the animation's dashoffset equal to the total path length (here ~370) so the loop is seamless.

effects.title: Jelly Dots
effects.summary: Three dots stretch and rebound on a springy cubic-bezier.
effects.description: An overshooting easing curve on scale plus a small vertical hop gives the dots elasticity without any physics library.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative status indicator — pair it with a visually-hidden aria-live message so screen readers announce the wait. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.ai_usage: Use when a plain three-dot loader feels too flat. The elasticity is entirely in cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1) — reuse that curve anywhere you want a spring without JS.

effects.title: Loading Ellipsis

effects.description: A label with animated trailing dots.

effects.title: Meshing Gears
effects.summary: Two SVG gears turn in opposite directions at speeds set by their tooth counts.

effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative status indicator — pair it with a visually-hidden aria-live message so screen readers announce the wait. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
variations: Pause on hover to inspect the mesh

effects.title: Metronome
effects.summary: A weighted arm swings between two stops with a click dot at each extreme.
effects.description: transform-origin at the base plus an ease-in-out swing produces pendulum motion; the flash at each end lands exactly at the keyframe extremes.

effects.title: Morphing Loader

effects.description: A shape cycling through square, circle, and triangle.

effects.title: Orbit Loader

effects.accessibility_notes: Wrap with role='status' and a visually-hidden 'Loading…' label so state is announced. Under prefers-reduced-motion, stop rotation (show a static atom).

effects.ai_usage: Use as a branded loading state for science/AI/dev products. Stack rings (each a bordered ellipse rotated in 3D) with a dot positioned on the edge; rotate each ring at a different --speed and direction; pulse the core. Wrap in role='status' + a visually-hidden 'Loading…' label and freeze rotation under prefers-reduced-motion.

Third orbit at a third speed

effects.title: Pac-Man Loader

effects.description: Two clipped half-circles hinge open and closed for the mouth while dots translate leftward on a loop and vanish at the bite point.

effects.title: Percent Counter Ring
effects.summary: A ring that fills while a number counts up in step with it.
effects.description: A conic-gradient angle and a text counter are driven by one requestAnimationFrame loop, so the label can never drift from the arc.
effects.accessibility_notes: Decorative status indicator — pair it with a visually-hidden aria-live message so screen readers announce the wait. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

effects.title: Ring Spinner

Dashed border for a tick ring
Slow spin for a calmer feel

Apply .spinner; the colored border-top-color + transparent other sides creates the arc, animation:spin 1s linear infinite rotates it. Always wrap with role=status and a visually-hidden 'Loading…' label. Size via --size; match --color to brand.

effects.title: Ripple Pulse

effects.title: Scanning Line

effects.description: A line sweeping across a placeholder block.

effects.title: Segmented Progress

effects.title: Spectrum Analyzer

effects.title: Spring Physics Easing
effects.summary: Spring curves as pure CSS linear() tokens, racing a plain ease-out so you can see the overshoot and settle.
effects.description: A cubic-bezier can never leave the 0–1 range on the way out, so it can ease but never overshoot. A damped spring can. Each lane here runs the same travel through a different timing function against a dashed target line: the ease-out lane stops dead on the line, while the spring lanes sail past it and settle back. The spring curves are sampled from a damped harmonic oscillator and baked into CSS linear() tokens, so they need no JavaScript and no animation library.
effects.browser_support: linear() easing: Chrome 113+, Firefox 112+, Safari 17.2+. Older browsers ignore the unknown timing function and fall back to the ease declared before it, so motion still happens, just without overshoot.
effects.performance_notes: Four compositor-friendly loops. linear() costs no more than a cubic-bezier — it is resolved once, not sampled per frame. Animating transform rather than left keeps every lane off the layout path.
effects.accessibility_notes: All motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion and each dot rests on its target. Overshoot draws the eye, so keep it for small, self-contained elements (toasts, badges, toggles) and off anything a user is reading or aiming at.

customization.name: --spring-gentle
customization.description: 8% overshoot, settles fast — the safe default for UI

customization.name: --spring-stiff
customization.description: 7% overshoot with a quicker settle — good for toggles and tabs

customization.name: --spring-bouncy
customization.description: 42% overshoot with visible secondary bounces — playful, use sparingly

customization.name: --travel
customization.description: How far the dot moves; overshoot is a multiple of this, so leave room after it

customization.name: duration
customization.description: Springs read as stiffer when shortened; retune damping rather than going below ~300ms

variations: Sample your own: x(t) = 1 - e^(-d·t)·(cos(w·t) + (d/w)·sin(w·t)), t from 0 to 1
Raise w for more oscillations, raise d to damp them out sooner
Apply to scale instead of translate for a pop-in
Pair with @starting-style for an entrance that springs on first paint
effects.ai_usage:
Use when motion should feel physical rather than merely timed — a toast landing, a toggle knob, a badge popping in, a card snapping to a grid slot. Store the three linear() values as --spring-gentle / --spring-stiff / --spring-bouncy tokens and reference them in animation or transition, exactly like a cubic-bezier token.

Pick by overshoot budget: gentle (8%) for anything routine, stiff (7%, faster settle) for state toggles, bouncy (42%) only for deliberate delight on small elements. The overshoot is a MULTIPLE of the animated distance, so a bouncy 300px slide overshoots by 126px — reserve the space or it clips.

Generate your own from a damped harmonic oscillator: x(t) = 1 - e^(-d*t)*(cos(w*t) + (d/w)*sin(w*t)) sampled evenly over t in [0,1]; higher w = more oscillations, higher d = faster damping. Pin the first sample to 0 and the last to 1 so the animation starts and ends exactly on its endpoints.

Avoid springing anything large or text-bearing (it induces motion sickness and hurts readability), springing a property that triggers layout (animate transform, not width/left/top), and springing an element the user is trying to click — it moves the target out from under the pointer. Always ship the reduced-motion guard.

effects.ai_usage: Use as primary navigation/search in apps and dev tools. Toggle a dialog on ⌘K/Ctrl+K AND a visible button; filter the command array on input; track a selected index for ArrowUp/Down + Enter; Esc closes and restores focus to the trigger. Wire ARIA: role='dialog' aria-modal, input with aria-activedescendant, listbox/options with aria-selected. Always offer a clickable trigger, not just the shortcut.
